messages:
sanjay: Heads-up: seeing a 12-18% p99 increase on INT8 weight-only after the AWQ calibration rollout on dedicated-prod-3. Dashboard: https://perf.redwood.internal/r/ai/p99?id=awq-rollout :eyes:
emma: Which variant was rolled? AWQ or GPTQ? Any change to group_size or packing config?
sanjay: AWQ only. Canary used group_size=16 (was 8 earlier) + enabled the new pack-alignment heuristic. Quick numbers from canary vs baseline:
```
baseline (group=8): p50=12ms p95=38ms p99=72ms
canary  (group=16): p50=11ms p95=42ms p99=83ms
packing_time median: +35%
```
ben: I repro'd locally on microbench. The slowdown is in the pack/unpack hotpath — extra memcpy when switching to the group-aware kernel. The kernel-selector now prefers the new group-16 kernel which returns buffers not in-place, so we do an extra copy.
hala: Also seeing a higher KV-cache eviction rate on the same runs. Likely alignment change causes more slab fragmentation and extra misses. KV eviction traces show more partial slabs: slot_density dropped ~12%.
deploy-bot: deploy to dedicated-prod-3 by emma at 2026-03-17T14:23:11Z (canary)
emma: Good catch. Is the memcpy coming from the packer, or the kernel API contract change?
ben: From what I can tell it's the kernel API — the new group kernel returns packed slices that aren't 64-byte aligned for our allocator, so the packer performs an align-copy. Patch diff: `kernel/group_pack_v2` changes return buffer ownership.
raj: I pushed the kernel-selector tweak last week to prefer group-wise kernels for AWQ workloads. The fallback path is supposed to be inplace, but for memory-aligned cases it falls back to the unpack path. I can revert selector preference for canary.
sana: I'll run a perf job on dedicated-prod-3: 100k requests, QPS=200, trace enabled. Will collect traces + p99 histograms and KV eviction logs. ETA ~1h.
emma: In parallel: ben, can you run microbench across group sizes [4,8,12,16] and include packing_time / memcpy_time and kernel_latencies? Put results in the perf gist.
ben: On it. Early numbers look like packing overhead grows roughly linearly with group size after 8. Will attach CSV.
sanjay: Possible next steps: 1) rollback selector preference on canary 2) add a quick allocator pinning to keep pack buffers aligned 3) longer-term: change kernel API to promise in-place for weight-only packs or add an optimized copy path that uses dma-friendly memcpy.
emma: Agreed. Also add gating in rollout: if p99 regresses >8% revert automatically. We didn't have that threshold turned on for this canary.
raj: Rolling back selector preference on canary now. Noting we need a test that simulates allocator alignment variety.
hala: I'll dig into KV allocator heuristics — maybe we can avoid splits by allowing pack buffers to be allocated from a dedicated slab class.
ben: Quick workaround: pin `group_size=8` for the next few hours to reduce impact. Also I'll prototype an aligned buffer pool to avoid copies.
sana: Perf job started. Traces show packing memcpy spikes correlated with p99 spikes. Uploading artifacts to /runs/2456789012.
sanjay: Thanks everyone. Assigning action items in the thread: raj -> rollback (done), ben -> aligned pool prototype, hala -> allocator variant, sana -> perf artifacts, emma -> rollout gating.
emma: Keep updates here. We'll re-evaluate once artifacts complete. :thumbsup:
file_notes: single slack thread: short messages, code snippets, perf links, deploy bot. Focus: AWQ int8 weight-only packing / group-size perf regression and triage.
